subject: CHEMISTRY

subtopics.title: Pressure, temperature, volume as experimental variables

slots.X: An idealised sealed piston holds a fixed amount of gas at 300 K. It initially moves against constant external pressure but reaches a rigid mechanical stop at 315 K; heating then continues to 330 K. Describe which variables change during each interval and calculate the final pressure relative to its value at the stop.
slots.Y: A piston may switch physical constraints during a continuous temperature change: first an approximately constant external-pressure expansion, then a fixed-volume phase against a stop. The valid law follows the interval and controlled variable, not a remembered formula alone. Draw two separate before/after state tables and check whether the amount of gas is genuinely conserved.
slots.Z: From 300 to 315 K, the piston moves at approximately constant pressure, so V_stop/V_initial = 315/300 = 1.05. Above 315 K the rigid stop fixes V and n; under the ideal-gas approximation P_final/P_stop = 330/315 ≈ 1.0476. It is wrong to treat the entire 300–330 K range as simultaneously constant pressure and fixed volume.
slots.W: Choose two consecutive thermodynamic constraint models rather than applying one gas rule throughout; distinguish the expansion and fixed-volume stages.

qrt_instances.wrong_idea: The pressure must stay constant for the entire heating because the piston could move at first.
qrt_instances.replacement_rule: Reject: The pressure must stay constant for the entire heating because the piston could move at first. Correct the missing constraint or species and verify a separate measurement.

qrt_instances.independent_check: If the piston leaks after reaching the stop, does P_final/P_stop still follow from temperatures alone?

slots.Z: The flexible balloon can expand as particles exert pressure, while rigid cylinder volume is fixed and pressure can rise. An ideal gas approximation works only when the amount is fixed and no condensation/reaction intervenes.

subtopics.title: Gas collection and measurement uncertainty

slots.X: Two reactions nominally produce equal moles of H₂ and CO₂, but each gas is collected separately over water. The recorded wet-gas volumes differ. Explain why the volume comparison alone cannot establish unequal chemical yields, and specify two controls or corrections that would test that interpretation.
slots.Y: Wet-gas volume is not equivalent to reaction yield. Compare a sparingly soluble collected gas and a more water-soluble one under matched generation conditions; decide which instrument and sampling observations would distinguish dissolution, leakage and genuine differences in production.
slots.Z: Measured gas over water contains vapour and may lose some target gas to dissolution, with CO₂ generally appreciably more soluble than H₂. Raw collection volumes cannot be equated to generated moles without matched T/P, water-vapour pressure corrections, dissolved-gas accounting and apparatus leak checks. Independent dry-gas collection or calibrated dissolved-CO₂ assessment can distinguish collection loss from a genuinely different reaction yield.
slots.W: Separate amount generated from wet-gas volume measured; account for water vapour, dissolution, temperature/pressure and possible leakage.

subtopics.title: Combustion gases and condensation

slots.X: For an idealised complete combustion, mix 1 mol propane (C₃H₈) with 6 mol O₂. Construct the atom-balanced reaction and calculate hot gas amounts, dry gas amounts after full water condensation, and remaining gas after selective CO₂ absorption. Explain which result changes if condensation is incomplete.
slots.Y: Before applying gas volumes to an unfamiliar hydrocarbon, balance its combustion equation and write separate hot-vapour, cooled-dry and absorber-residue ledgers. A phase change redistributes atoms between gas and liquid, not outside the material conservation law.
slots.Z: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. Six moles O₂ initially leave 1 mol excess oxygen. Before cooling, gaseous CO₂ 3 + water vapour 4 + O₂ 1 = 8 mol (under stated hot-gas assumption). After full condensation, dry gas is 3 mol CO₂ plus 1 mol O₂ = 4 mol; selective CO₂ removal leaves 1 mol O₂. If water remains as vapour, the supposed 'dry' gas total and contraction differ; the condensation assumption is critical.
slots.W: Derive a new hydrocarbon's O₂ requirement and track separate gas-phase inventories through cooling and selective absorption.

Explain which result changes if condensation is incomplete.
qrt_instances.wrong_idea: All water produced disappears from the entire system on cooling, so atoms are not conserved.
qrt_instances.replacement_rule: Reject: All water produced disappears from the entire system on cooling, so atoms are not conserved. Correct the missing constraint or species and verify a separate measurement.

subtopics.title: Gas absorption sequences and eudiometry (enrichment)

slots.X: An ideal eudiometry mixture contains 8 mL CH₄, 4 mL inert N₂ and 24 mL O₂ at the same reference T/P. After complete combustion and cooling to condense water, the dry volume reads 20 mL. After selective CO₂ removal it reads 12 mL. Check these readings with a species ledger and decide whether the final 12 mL can be labelled oxygen alone; propose a discriminating measurement.
slots.Y: A selective absorber removes its target, not all other gases. An unreactive carrier or air contaminant may persist alongside unconsumed O₂; a final instrument reading therefore needs an independent gas-identity check before inferring a pure residual species.
slots.Z: 8 mL CH₄ consumes 16 mL O₂, produces 8 mL CO₂ and 16 mL water vapour at matched reference gas conditions. The remaining 8 mL O₂ and original 4 mL N₂ are nonabsorbed. After complete water condensation: 8 CO₂ + 8 O₂ + 4 N₂ = 20 mL dry. After selective CO₂ removal: 8 O₂ + 4 N₂ = 12 mL. An oxygen-specific assay or separate inert-gas analysis is needed; total post-absorber volume is not equivalent to oxygen amount.
slots.W: Independently separate combustible gas, oxygen excess, carbon dioxide and an inert gas across stages, rejecting the assumption that all post-absorber gas is O₂.

qrt_instances.replacement_rule: Reject: Every gas remaining after selective CO₂ absorption must be oxygen. Correct the missing constraint or species and verify a separate measurement.
